papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes under sparse radiosonde initialization: a climate-analytics evaluation of tail-index distortion in dam-safety analytics
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.

papers.title: Active-learning prioritization of rain-gauge densification under budget constraints: a computer-science evaluation of flood-forecast skill gain per instrument dollar
papers.abstract: Rain-gauge networks in data-sparse basins are typically densified by spatial coverage criteria rather than by the marginal value of each additional instrument to flood-forecast skill. the present analysis formalises gauge densification as a sequential decision problem in which a learner selects the next gauge location from a candidate set, observes a proxy label, and updates a surrogate of forecast-relevant rainfall error, subject to a fixed budget. We derive a cost-normalised active-learning criterion, the marginal skill gain per instrument dollar, and show that under a submodular surrogate the greedy policy admits a constant-factor approximation guarantee relative to the optimal budget-feasible subset. The framework is evaluated on a real reanalysis record for Kampala, Uganda: NASA POWER monthly MERRA-2 air temperature at 2 m, 312 monthly observations from 2000 to 2023, with mean 22.443 C, standard deviation 1.043 C, and a linear trend of -0.1564 C per decade. The trend is small relative to interannual variability, which we use to motivate the variance-reduction objective that the active learner optimises. We report the design of the prioritisation procedure, the approximation bound, and the conditions under which cost-normalised greedy selection diverges from coverage-maximising selection. The contribution is a computer-science formalisation of instrument placement as budgeted active learning, with an explicit skill-per-dollar objective and a provable guarantee, rather than a new empirical forecast study.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled bioprinting for tumor modeling: from biomimetic microenvironment reconstruction to drug screening
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting have provided new strategies for developing in vitro tumor models with improved representation of native tumor microenvironments. This review examines the role of AI across the entire bioprinting workflow—from image-based model design and real-time printing control to post-printing functional assessment and high-throughput drug evaluation. We first outline how machine learning and deep learning algorithms optimize bioink formulation, predict the mechanical behavior of printed constructs, and enable error correction during fabrication. We then discuss AI-driven strategies for reconstructing key components of the tumor microenvironment, including extracellular matrices with tunable mechanical properties, perfusable vascular networks, and spatially organized multi-cellular architectures that incorporate cancer cells, stromal cells, and immune populations. The review further addresses the application of AI-enhanced bioprinted tumor models in automated drug screening, resistance mechanism studies, and personalized medicine, with particular attention to the integration of patient-derived cells and multi-omics data. We also evaluate current challenges, including the trade-off between biomimetic fidelity and throughput, the lack of standardized protocols and data repositories, and the need for improved model validation against clinical outcomes. Finally, we discuss emerging directions such as closed-loop optimization systems, intelligent bioinks, and the integration of bioprinting with organ-on-a-chip platforms. By providing a comprehensive overview of this rapidly evolving field, this review aims to inform researchers and clinicians about the current capabilities and future potential of AI-assisted bioprinted tumor models for oncology research and therapeutic development.

papers.title: Enhancing the bending performance of SLA-printed TPMS sandwich structures through the core topology optimization
papers.abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) structures, e.g., Diamond (D), Gyroid (G), and I-WP, possess excellent specific strength and geometric designability, thereby achieving high load-bearing capacity and lightweight design. However, when serving as the core in sandwich structures, the uniform relative density (uni-den) design and conventionally functionally graded (con-fun-gra) design do not fully utilize the mechanical properties of materials. To overcome this limitation, a variable-density topology optimization (var-top-opt) design is adopted in the D, G, and I-WP cores to enhance the bending performance of sandwich structures, and the enhancement effects are explored. The fitting functions between the isosurface threshold and relative density are constructed for the D, G, and I-WP cells. The var-top-opt design, taking the relative density of the topology element as the design variable and the structural compliance minimization as the design objective, is performed to obtain the optimal relative density field (ORDF). The ORDF is divided into multiple segments, and the relative densities in every segment are fitted to construct the relative density function matrix of topology elements. The isosurface threshold function matrices of the optimized D, G, and I-WP cores are constructed through the relative density mapping relationship between the topology elements and TPMS cells. The D, G, and I-WP sandwich structures from the uni-den, con-fun-gra, and var-top-opt designs are fabricated using the SLA technology, followed by the three-point bending test and numerical simulation. The results show that the var-top-opt design significantly enhances the bending stiffness and energy absorption of the TPMS sandwich structures at different core volume fractions, and the improvement is larger than that of the con-fun-gra design.

papers.title: Biomechanical and fatigue analysis of a porous titanium total temporomandibular joint prosthesis with different mandibular component lengths and designs.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the biomechanical behavior and fatigue lifetime of Voronoi lattice-structured ramus components for total temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) in mini (mini-TMJR), standard (TMJR), and extended (eTMJR) configurations based on the Walter Lorenz (Biomet) system, using finite element analysis. Three-dimensional models were derived from Visible Human Project computed tomography data. For each ramus length, four designs were analyzed: Voronoi architectures with 25%, 50%, and 75% filling ratios, and a fully solid design, under masticatory forces simulating unilateral left molar clenching. Von Mises stress, principal bone stress, and fatigue safety factors were evaluated. Ramus stress decreased with increasing filling ratio, ranging from 363.5 MPa (TMJR 25% Voronoi) to 71.3 MPa (eTMJR solid); all designs showed infinite fatigue life, with safety factors of 1.5-7.8. Fossa and ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) stresses increased with filling ratio, with UHMWPE stress exceeding the polyethylene yield strength in all models, while bone stress remained within physiological limits. Low filling ratio designs transferred more load to bone, which may reduce stress shielding, whereas the eTMJR solid design showed the lowest ramus stress and highest safety factor. Voronoi-latticed ramus components showed acceptable biomechanical performance under the simulated conditions, though long-term biological and clinical validation is required.

papers.title: Mechano-adaptive regenerative niches for orchestrating functional reinnervation of peripheral nerve defects
papers.abstract: Abstract Transcending the paradigm of passive structural support, contemporary peripheral nerve repair pivots decisively toward the deliberate spatiotemporal programming of instructive microenvironments. Integrative evidence, synthesized from bibliometric landscapes and high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic atlases, has firmly established mechanotransduction as a preeminent regulatory hub, while concurrently resolving the injury-elicited mechanosensitive phenotypic landscapes. This evidence informs a mechano-adaptive niche-engineering framework that systematically deciphers how biophysical cues govern Schwann cell plasticity, directed axonal navigation, macrophage phenotypic re-polarization, vascular integration, and global tissue homeostasis. In this context, advanced additive manufacturing platforms, notably three- and four-dimensional biofabrication, serve as foundational cornerstones for constructing biomimetic niches endowed with spatiotemporally programmable and dynamically interactive features. Collectively, these mechanistic insights are rigorously codified into rational design blueprints, wherein stiffness gradients, topographical anisotropy, and dynamic mechanical actuation converge to define next-generation neural guidance conduits. In their clinical translation, adaptive, patient-conformal, and context-responsive biofabrication ecosystems constitute transformative modalities, propelling mechano-regenerative biomaterials toward a new vanguard in neural reinnervation.

papers.title: 3D bioprinting of tissue-engineered bladder patches containing neurovascular networks using conductive microgel
papers.abstract: Current tissue-engineered bladder patches are hindered by the absence of coordinated neurovascular regeneration, which limits their functional repair capacity. This study aimed to develop a neurovascularized bladder patch (NVBP) and assess its efficacy in bladder defect repair. GelMA-MXene (GM) conductive hydrogel microspheres encapsulating adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) were initially prepared to induce efficient differentiation of ADSCs into neural and vascular lineages within a conductive microenvironment. These pre-differentiated neural and vascular microspheres were then formulated into a microgel bioink, facilitating the construction of the NVBP using 3D bioprinting technology. Results indicated that GM microspheres enhanced ADSCs viability, proliferation, and stemness markers (Sox2/Nanog). Upon induction, GM microspheres upregulated the expression of neural-related genes (TUBB3, MAP2, Nestin, GAP43) and vascular-related genes (KDR, ANGPT1). Transcriptomic analysis and validation results demonstrated that the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway was significantly enriched, and the expression of Tnn and Pik3cd genes within it was also upregulated. This pathway might contribute to the effect on MXene’s promotion of ADSCs’ differentiation into neural and vascular lineages. The microgel bioink exhibited shear-thinning behavior, a broad printing temperature range, and excellent self-healing and fatigue resistance. The 3D bioprinted NVBP effectively maintained stable neural and vascular phenotypes. In an in vivo rat model, NVBP significantly enhanced bladder capacity (923.76 ± 119.80 µL) and compliance (27.04 ± 5.22 µL/mmHg). Histological analysis revealed improved smooth muscle organization, reduced collagen deposition, and significantly increased areas positive for βIII-Tubulin, PECAM1, and α-SMA in the NVBP group. In summary, NVBP promotes rat bladder tissue remodeling and functional recovery through synergistic neurovascular regeneration, offering a novel biomimetic strategy for bladder tissue engineering and is worthy of further in-depth research. 3D bioprinting of tissue-engineered bladder patches containing neurovascular networks using conductive microgel

papers.title: When active learning fails, uncalibrated out of distribution uncertainty quantification might be the problem
papers.abstract: Abstract Efficiently and meaningfully estimating prediction uncertainty is important for exploration in active learning campaigns in materials discovery, where samples with high uncertainty are interpreted as containing information missing from the model. In this work, the effect of different uncertainty estimation and calibration methods are evaluated for active learning when using ensembles of ALIGNN, eXtreme Gradient Boost, Random Forest, and Neural Network model architectures. We compare uncertainty estimates from ALIGNN deep ensembles to loss landscape uncertainty estimates obtained for solubility, bandgap, and formation energy prediction tasks. We then evaluate how the quality of the uncertainty estimate impacts an active learning campaign that seeks model generalization to out-of-distribution data. Uncertainty calibration methods were found to variably generalize from in-domain data to out-of-domain data. Furthermore, calibrated uncertainties were generally unsuccessful in reducing the amount of data required by a model to improve during an active learning campaign on out-of-distribution data when compared to random sampling and uncalibrated uncertainties. The impact of poor-quality uncertainty persists for random forest and eXtreme Gradient Boosting models trained on the same data for the same tasks, indicating that this is at least partially intrinsic to the data and not due to model capacity alone. Analysis of the target, in-distribution uncertainty, out-of-distribution uncertainty, and training residual distributions suggest that future work focus on understanding empirical uncertainties in the feature input space for cases where ensemble prediction variances do not accurately capture the missing information required for the model to generalize.

papers.title: Evaluating regression models and machine learning for long-term energy demand forecasting – Germany
papers.abstract: Reliable long-term energy demand forecasting underpins energy-system planning and decarbonization policy design, yet most established methods are calibrated for short horizons and may not capture structural change. This study compares four forecasting models: multiple linear regression (MLR), a vector error correction model (VECM), support vector regression (SVR), and an artificial neural network (ANN). Germany’s final energy consumption (FEC) is projected to 2050 from annual data spanning 1992–2021. The SVR and ANN were tuned using particle swarm optimization and Bayesian optimization. Accuracy is assessed using mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), and the coefficient of determination (R²). The switching term in Adaptive Sliding Mode Control(ASMC)’s control law causes high-frequency jitter. To address this, this paper proposes an intelligent cooperative control strategy based on a Genetic Algorithm (GA)-optimized MPC. By incorporating real-world physical constraints (such as actuator saturation) and industrial duty-cycle requirements, a nonlinear dynamic model with load-swing coupling is established. A dual-objective MPC framework is then constructed, leveraging GA to eliminate manual tuning dependency and achieve global optimization. The strategy’s applicability to common industrial scenarios is validated through multi-scenario simulations under stochastic variations in rope lengths and payload masses. Results demonstrate that the strategy significantly enhances performance—reducing tracking errors by 32.74% and swing angles by 14.44%, while lowering control energy consumption, offering a reliable, and generalizable solution for fully autonomous material handling systems.

Methods A 9.3 μm CO 2 laser osteotomy platform was developed by combining controlled pulse-overlap scanning with gas-atomized water-mist cooling. The generated osteotomy interfaces were characterized in terms of surface topography, thermal response, microstructural preservation, and local mechanical integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSC) alignment, focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, osteogenic differentiation, and osteoclast formation were evaluated in vitro. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were performed to investigate the underlying molecular programs. The optimized interface was further assessed in a rat femoral defect model with porous titanium scaffold implantation. Results The laser osteotomy strategy generated deterministic microscale grooves and graded nanoscale roughness, forming anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano osteotomy interfaces. Compared with mechanical cutting, laser osteotomy reduced thermal accumulation, limited microstructural disruption, and better maintained local mechanical integrity. The engineered interfaces directed hMSC alignment and activated focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, as indicated by enhanced pFAK activation, Lamin A/C reinforcement, and YAP nuclear translocation. These responses promoted osteogenic differentiation and suppressed osteoclast formation, with the Laser III group showing the most favorable biological response. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed enrichment of adhesion-, cytoskeleton-, and PI3K-Akt-related osteogenic programs. In vivo, the optimized interface enhanced peri-implant bone regeneration, mineral apposition, and osseointegration. Conclusions This study provides proof-of-concept evidence that 9.3 μm CO 2 laser osteotomy may enable bone cutting to be coupled with in situ regenerative interface engineering. By reducing cutting-associated damage and actively programming the host bone interface, this approach shows translational potential for improving peri-implant bone healing and implant integration. The translational potential of this article 9.3 μm CO 2 laser-enabled osteotomy interface engineering integrates precise bone cutting with in situ programming of the host bone surface. This study reveals that laser-generated anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano interfaces can reduce cutting-associated damage, activate adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, promote osteogenic differentiation, suppress osteoclast maturation, and enhance peri-implant osseointegration. papers.title: Δ-HGPR: A Hierarchical Gaussian Process Framework for Active-Learning Δ-Potentials
papers.abstract: Abstract Δ-learning, which uses machine learning to represent only the difference between a high-accuracy reference and a lower-accuracy base calculator, is a promising route to high-fidelity molecular dynamics (MD) with limited training data, but it has lacked a unified protocol combining hierarchical descriptors with well-defined equilibrium sampling. We propose Δ-HGPR (hierarchical Gaussian process regression for Δ-learning), a framework for learning difference potentials, and its MD instantiation, Δ-HGPR-MD. The framework combines (i) a difference potential written as an additive radial (inverse-distance) term plus a many-body machine-learning correction, determined by a single regularized least-squares fit; (ii) the ensemble force standard deviation as an active-learning indicator with an automatically scaled threshold; and (iii) a difference potential held fixed within each round so that equilibrium NVT sampling is well-defined in both exploration and production. The many-body term of Δ-HGPR-MD uses smooth overlap of atomic positions (SOAP) descriptors with random Fourier features (Δ-HGPR-RFF). On a toy system whose difference potential contains a 1/r contribution beyond the cutoff of the local descriptor, the many-body term alone reproduces none of this force, however many features it is given, whereas the hierarchy recovers 99% of it, with a reach set by the cutoff of its radial term. In MD, the hierarchy reproduces about 80% of the shift of the ion-pair distribution toward the reference, while the many-body term alone leaves it where the base places it. On malonaldehyde and the Zundel cation H5O2+ with three base calculators, Δ-HGPR-RFF removes barrier errors of up to 0.1 eV under one protocol, giving free-energy barriers statistically indistinguishable from DFT; free-energy perturbation shows that the error contributed by the learned correction is below 0.01 eV on average in every case. For H5O2+with ANI-2x, whose dynamics collapse without correction, it recovers the Zundel geometry and a barrier and transition count consistent with DFT.

papers.abstract: Abstract While monitoring biodiversity through camera traps has become an important endeavour for ecological research, identifying species in the captured image data remains a major bottleneck due to limited labelling resources. Active learning—a machine learning paradigm that selects the most informative data to label and train a predictive model—offers a promising solution, but typically focuses on uncertainty in the individual predictions without considering uncertainty across the entire dataset. We study Vendi information gain (VIG) as an active learning policy that selects images based on their impact on dataset‐wide prediction uncertainty, capturing both informativeness and diversity. We applied VIG to two representative datasets in ecological image classification, the Kenya Camera Trap Dataset and the Missouri Camera Trap dataset, and compared VIG against common active learning methods. On both datasets, VIG achieves higher accuracy with fewer labelled examples. We further conducted extensive ablation studies to investigate the effects of the predictive model, batch sizes and other hyperparameters to find relatively robust performance from VIG. VIG has broad applicability beyond ecology, and our results highlight its value for biodiversity monitoring in data‐limited environments.

papers.title: AI and Intelligent Building Analytics for Energy Efficiency in Large Healthcare Campuses
papers.abstract: Large healthcare campuses contain dissimilar clinical and non-clinical buildings, central thermal plants and increasingly connected building-control systems. Their energy demand is unusually difficult to optimise because continuity of care, infection prevention, thermal conditions and equipment reliability constrain operational flexibility. This critical narrative review evaluates whether artificial intelligence and intelligent building analytics offer credible improvements in energy efficiency at the campus scale, and under what technical and governance conditions. Peer-reviewed hospital-specific investigations, building-energy prediction and fault-detection studies, field evaluations of predictive control, and research on digital twins and clinical indoor environments were critically synthesised. Evidence available through 12 August 2026 was considered. The literature supports a clear distinction between accurate energy forecasting, detection of actionable faults, and measured energy savings attributable to closed-loop interventions. Hospital data studies demonstrate promising predictive performance, whereas direct, prolonged, independently evaluated deployments across entire healthcare campuses remain uncommon. Model predictive control has a stronger real-building implementation record than autonomous reinforcement learning, but aggregate benefits from ordinary commercial buildings cannot be assumed to apply to operating theatres, isolation rooms or critical services. In addition, normalisation by clinical activity, sensor calibration, counterfactual measurement, interoperability and cybersecurity materially influence the validity of claimed savings. This review proposes a safety-constrained, hierarchical approach in which transparent benchmarking and diagnostics precede supervised optimisation and carefully governed campus-level coordination. Future investigations should report whole-campus and zone-level outcomes, seasonal persistence, uncertainty, clinical environmental compliance, equipment reliability and carbon consequences under reproducible evaluation designs. Intelligent analytics should therefore be understood as a means of improving the quality of operational decisions rather than an independently established guarantee of hospital energy savings.

The SMC formulates a sliding surface combining yaw rate error and sideslip angle error, deploying a boundary-layer saturation function to eliminate chattering while preserving robust stability margins under nonlinear tire dynamics and variable road friction. The efficiency-aware torque allocator pre-computes optimal torque-speed operating regions offline and retrieves them via a 2D lookup table at each control step, achieving multi-objective performance simultaneous stability enhancement and energy efficiency improvementwithout requiring any online optimization. Comparative MATLAB/Simulink evaluation under a standardized step-steer maneuver at 60 km/h on a dry surface (μ = 0.85) demonstrates that the proposed SMC reduces yaw rate root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 51.2% relative to the proportional (P) baseline, by 33.5% relative to PID, and by 37.6% relative to the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR), while consuming only 139.8 kJ compared to the highest-consumption controller at 142.7 kJ. papers.title: Temporally Gated Active Thermography for Defect Detection in Laser-Based Powder Bed Fusion of Metals
papers.abstract: Abstract Laser Powder Bed Fusion of Metal is a key additive manufacturing technology, but its industrial adoption is limited by inherent process imperfections. While in-situ non-destructive testing is essential, current monitoring methods face limitations. In-line active thermography, as a promising testing approach, faces significant challenges with overpowering reflections from the high-energy process laser, which can saturate sensors and mask faint, defect-related thermal emissions. This paper introduces a novel stroboscopic active thermography methodology designed to overcome this limitation. The approach utilizes the Synchronized Path Infrared Thermography dual scanhead setup, which employs the processing laser as a modulated thermal excitation source. This system is based on precise temporal gating of the acquisition of the IR camera: it isolates the desired thermal emission signal from interfering laser reflections, and it ensures that the same, specific segment of the material cooling curve is consistently sampled for every measurement point. The stroboscopic approach was validated on specimens with artificial subsurface defects. It successfully eliminates sensor saturation, providing a high-fidelity thermal signal for analysis. The system identifies voids with actual mean diameters as small as 111 $$\upmu $$ μ m at depths of down to 40 $$\upmu $$ μ m. The study also quantifies the technical boundaries of the method, where signal attenuation from thermal diffusion limits detection at 120 $$\upmu $$ μ m depth to the largest defect measuring 977 $$\upmu $$ μ m.

papers.title: AI-Driven Acoustic Metamaterial Optimization for Broadband Noise Control
papers.abstract: The acoustic metamaterials have some transformational advantages in terms of noise reduction, but it is still a challenge to design them to be broadband. Conventional design methodologies are based on parametric sweeps and trial-error system, not effective to the complicated metamaterial geometries. The paper presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-based design methodology of broadband acoustic metamaterials inverse optimization. In a hybrid approach, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is combined with finite element simulations to discover, with ease, design spaces and estimate by trial and error structures with small area of search that obtain desired acoustic performances over broader frequency bands. The framework uses surrogate model through neural networks which minimizes the computational expenses allowing evaluation of candidate geometries quickly. Examples of case studies are the design of labyrinthine panels and locally resonant metal panels used in aircraft engines noise and industrial machines. Findings show the highest sound transmission loss to the conventional designs with the optimized geometries that are tunable as well as structurally robust. The uniqueness of this study is the integration of AI with computational acoustics to limit the drawback of manual design, which can offer a scaling channel of broadband noise control solutions. The framework not only makes the process of metamaterial discovery faster but it also creates a pipeline that allows replication of AI integration in the engineering of computational acoustics.

papers.abstract: The initial fixation of the acetabular cup is crucial for outcomes in total hip arthroplasty (THA); however, stability is evaluated subjectively. We developed a Laser Resonance Frequency Analysis (Laser-RFA) system using low-output laser-induced vibration to objectively assess fixation. This study demonstrates the relationship between fixation strength and vibrational characteristics and evaluates surgeons' tactile assessment. In laboratory experiments, acetabular cups were press-fit into polyurethane simulated bone and stimulated with frequency-swept laser irradiation (preliminary laboratory experiment: 1500-4500 Hz; modified-condition: 2250-2750 Hz). Peak frequencies measured by the Laser Doppler vibrometer were correlated with fixation strength. In the clinical study, peak frequencies from microphone-recorded vibrations were compared between cases with and without screw fixation based on intraoperative tactile assessment. In a supplemental experiment, surgeons were divided into skilled and non-skilled groups. Participants implanted an acetabular cup into simulated bone, and tactile fixation strength was quantified. Periodic waveforms were identified in the preliminary experiment, and six peaks (Waves A-F) were defined in the modified-condition laboratory experiment. Waves A and B showed negative correlations with fixation strength, whereas Waves C-F showed positive correlations. Clinically, peak frequencies were lower in cases requiring screw fixation than in those not requiring screw fixation (approximately 2900 vs. 3050 Hz; p < 0.003). The supplemental experiment showed significant differences in fixation strength across all tactile assessment levels in the skilled group, whereas no significant differences were observed in the non-skilled group. These findings indicate Laser-RFA objectively assesses acetabular cup fixation and reflects the tactile assessment of experienced surgeons.

papers.abstract: Background: Conventional safe zones are defined by the proximity of acetabular cup screws to intrapelvic vessels; however, this relationship varies among individuals. This study aimed to define the intraosseous safe zone in which the screws remain entirely within bone without penetrating the medial wall. Methods: Three-dimensional computed tomography data for 30 hips of female patients with normal acetabular morphology were analyzed. A hemispherical cup was positioned virtually, and screw trajectories were evaluated in 24 directions using a clock-face coordinate system referenced to the ipsilateral anterior superior iliac spine. Bone thickness was measured in each direction, and intraosseous safe zones were defined for screw lengths of 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, and 50 mm. Heatmaps were generated to visualize the distribution of safe regions, and the angular range in which screws remained intraosseous in all cases was determined. Results: The median patient age was 50.1 years. The intraosseous safe zone was consistently located in the posterosuperior region for all screw lengths. The extent of the safe zone significantly decreased as the screw length increased (p < 0.01), whereas shorter screws expanded the safe zone toward the posteroinferior region. The angular range of the intraosseous safe zone was consistently the greatest at the 11 and 11:30 o'clock positions for 15, 20, and 25 mm screws. Conclusions: The findings provide a useful framework for preoperative planning and conceptualizing safe screw trajectories in total hip arthroplasty. Clinical Relevance: Directing screws toward the posterosuperior acetabulum, particularly around the 11 o'clock region, may enhance safety by maintaining intraosseous fixation and avoiding intrapelvic neurovascular injury. Shorter screws may expand safe fixation options toward the posteroinferior region.

papers.title: Parameter estimation of the hybrid GPR-GAM model for climate data
papers.abstract: Climate data present significant challenges for statistical modelling because of nonlinear relationships among climatic variables and the presence of spatial dependence. Conventional parametric models may be inadequate for representing complex nonlinear covariate effects, while non-parametric approaches may not adequately account for residual spatial dependence. This study develops a unified parameter-estimation framework for the hybrid Gaussian Process Regression–Generalized Additive Model (GPR–GAM), building on the hybrid modelling formulation established in previous work. The proposed framework combines penalized generalized least squares (PGLS) for estimation of the GAM coefficients, best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) for the latent spatial process, and restricted maximum likelihood (REML) for estimation of the Gaussian process covariance, residual variance, and smoothing parameters. Closed-form expressions for the principal estimators are derived, and an L-BFGS-based numerical optimization procedure is presented for estimation of the hyperparameters. Simulation results indicate small empirical biases in the parameter estimates, with empirical 95% confidence-interval coverage probabilities ranging from 0.932 to 0.955. Application to Kenyan climate data produced statistically significant covariate effects and non-negligible spatial and residual variance components, demonstrating the ability of the framework to quantify both systematic covariate effects and residual spatial dependence. The proposed framework therefore provides a coherent basis for parameter estimation and uncertainty assessment in hybrid GPR–GAM models, with potential applications to climate modelling in regions characterised by complex topography and substantial climatic variability.

papers.abstract: The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples (N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability. People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between.

The manufacturing cell comprised six interconnected stations: raw-material inspection and sorting, automated loading and orientation, CNC machining, drilling and cutting, AI-assisted quality inspection, and automated storage and dispatch. A synchronized DT represented machine states, production flow, queue formation, operating parameters, energy consumption, tool condition, vibration, temperature, and quality outcomes. An AI layer supported anomaly detection and cycle-time prediction, while a multi-objective optimization mechanism balanced throughput and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) against cycle time, energy consumption, defect rate, and unplanned downtime. Three operating configurations were evaluated: conventional programmable logic controller (PLC)-based operation, DT-assisted operation, and DT–AI optimization. During the six-hour production period, the DT–AI configuration increased throughput from 338 to 405 parts, reduced average cycle time from 63.9 to 53.3 s/part, and increased OEE from 67.6% to 84.6%. Energy consumption decreased from 54.8 to 47.6 kWh, the defect rate declined from 5.9% to 2.6%, and unplanned downtime decreased from 38.4 to 17.9 min. The anomaly classifier achieved an accuracy of 94.6%, while the cycle-time prediction model achieved a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.94. These findings demonstrate the potential of DT–AI integration to improve productivity, energy efficiency, and operational reliability under the evaluated conditions. The framework offers a practical basis for progressive digital transformation in Bangladeshi mechanical manufacturing facilities, with further validation needed to establish its applicability across other production environments.

We also discuss challenges related to imbalanced datasets and the statistical techniques used to address them, providing insights into the reliability and generalizability of ML/DL models for AD diagnosis and prognosis.

papers.title: Classical and Bayesian Inference for the New Lindley-X Time Model Under Random Beta-Binomial Progressive First-Failure Censoring: Theory, Computation, and Cancer Survival Applications
papers.abstract: Incomplete lifetime observations arising from random subject withdrawals remain a major challenge in modern reliability and biomedical studies, where conventional progressive censoring schemes often fail to capture the stochastic nature of patient dropout and experimental interruption. Motivated by this limitation, this article develops a unified Bayesian inferential framework for the recently proposed one-parameter New XL (New-XL) lifetime distribution under a random beta-binomial progressive first-failure (B-Bin-PFF) censoring strategy. Both frequentist and Bayesian methodologies are developed for estimating the model parameter with the associated reliability and hazard rate functions. The derivation of maximum likelihood estimators includes two asymptotic confidence intervals, as well as Bayesian estimation accompanied by two credible intervals. Since the posterior distributions are analytically intractable, posterior inference is performed through a Metropolis–Hastings Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm under independent gamma priors. An extensive Monte Carlo study investigates the finite-sample performance of the proposed procedures across a wide range of sample sizes, censoring proportions, group structures, and random withdrawal scenarios. The proposed methodology is finally illustrated using two clinically important cancer survival datasets involving gastric cancer and leukemia patients. The empirical analyses demonstrate that the proposed Bayesian framework provides accurate estimation, reliable uncertainty quantification, and superior goodness-of-fit compared with several competing lifetime models.

papers.title: TurboWAM: Learning What Matters for Fast World Action Models
papers.abstract: World action models have demonstrated promising performance in robot policy learning, yet their high inference latency remains a critical bottleneck for real-world deployment. However, these methods often leverage representations from all video world model layers without explicitly considering their varying relevance to action prediction, leading to redundant computation and suboptimal representation utilization. In this work, we propose TurboWAM, a fast world action model that efficiently aggregates structured world representations conditioned on action predictions. Specifically, TurboWAM introduces a structured world representation aggregation module that adaptively fuses representations from different world model layers according to their relevance to the evolving action denoising state. Furthermore, TurboWAM employs a structured action supervision mechanism that adaptively modulates gradients from action supervision across different world model layers during backward propagation, facilitating world representation learning. During inference, by reducing the number of world model layers executed and caching relevant representations across action denoising steps, TurboWAM substantially reduces computational overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that TurboWAM achieves low inference latency while maintaining competitive task success rates compared with state-of-the-art methods.

By executing matched action sequences in both the simulator and the world model, WMEval enables evaluation at both the perceptual level and the physical-causal level, using simulator-derived states as reference. papers.title: An actively trained neural operator for near-explicit atmospheric chemistry
papers.abstract: Earth-system models simplify atmospheric chemistry into condensed mechanisms, because near-explicit mechanisms such as the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM) are too costly to solve in every grid cell. The same network also guides its own training, using the disagreement among its experts to select the most informative box-model simulations. At equal cost, this active sampling yields a more accurate emulator than random or evenly spread sampling. Fine-tuning on longer trajectories keeps it stable over multi-hour runs in which models trained on short simulations diverge. The resulting emulator reproduces the evolution of thousands of species with high fidelity, remains accurate for unseen chemical compositions and runs orders of magnitude faster than the numerical solver. These results open a new direction for emulating complex atmospheric systems: neural operators that predict the full chemical state over long windows and choose their own training data. Training under changing meteorology is the next step towards bringing near-explicit chemistry into Earth-system models.

papers.title: Latent dynamics for reconstructing fine-scale PDE trajectories from coarse observations
papers.abstract: Coarse PDE observations omit spatial detail and intermediate states of evolving fields. We present Structured Latent Dynamics (SLD), a framework that reconstructs high-resolution trajectories from spatially and temporally downsampled simulations. SLD interpolates the input in time, adds a learned temporal correction and uses the resulting sequence to guide a hidden state on the coarse grid. Each update of the latent state combines a learned gated response with horizontal and vertical central differences and a five-point Laplacian of the state. The three spatial terms have learned channel-wise coefficients. Two Haar wavelet synthesis branches map the hidden state and refined coarse input to the high-resolution field. We evaluate SLD on two-dimensional Gray--Scott, complex Ginzburg--Landau and viscous Burgers systems, reconstructing 100 output frames from 25 input frames with eightfold refinement in each spatial direction. SLD achieves lower mean relative $L_2$ error and mean absolute error than unstructured latent dynamics and ConvLSTM baselines with comparable parameter counts, both on held-out trajectories and on later windows of trajectories used during training. SLD also reduces errors in regions with large reference gradients and across most or all of the evaluated later time intervals. A representative Gray--Scott comparison shows lower spectral error over most intermediate and high wavenumbers. Removing the fixed spatial response increased reconstruction error, supporting its contribution to the SLD architecture.

papers.title: A Differentiable Framework for Inverse Identification of Heterogeneous Cohesive Laws
papers.abstract: This work develops a differentiable finite element framework based on an intrinsic cohesive-zone formulation for identifying traction-separation laws from global force-displacement histories and spatially sparse strain measurements. The framework employs physics-constrained neural networks to represent flexible, thermodynamically structured cohesive laws, with sensitivities computed through automatic differentiation and a discrete adjoint that accounts for the history-dependent evolution of interfacial damage. To enable identification of spatially heterogeneous cohesive behavior, we extend learned constitutive priors to irreversible interfacial damage by constructing a shared, low-dimensional family of cohesive laws from representative traction-separation histories. This representation exploits common constitutive structure and parameter sharing to reduce the number of unknowns and regularize the inverse problem, while allowing local cohesive behavior to vary spatially through latent coordinates. Numerical investigations involving double-cantilever beams and fiber-matrix composites demonstrate that accurate reproduction of global force-displacement responses does not necessarily imply accurate recovery of the underlying cohesive laws. Incorporating spatially resolved strain measurements substantially improves constitutive identification, even when the admissible responses are constrained by a learned prior. Comparisons with conventional bilinear cohesive models and Bayesian optimization further illustrate the benefits of the learned constitutive representation and adjoint-based identification for high-dimensional inverse problems.

Spectral Hamiltonian Algebraic Power Evaluation (SHAPE) combines port-Hamiltonian variables and differential flatness to generate nominal power references from planned motion for fully actuated mechanical systems with collocated actuation. Subtracting these references from commanded effort multiplied by measured flow yields residuals whose final evaluation requires neither recursive observer updates nor measured-state dynamics calculations. Continuous wavelet transform (CWT) scalograms and a shared-encoder convolutional neural network are used to distinguish nominal operation, actuator loss of effectiveness, anomalous friction, and vibration from complete trajectories. Evaluation uses a simulated six degree of freedom Kinova manipulator under model predictive control and fixed plant-model mismatch, with single faults at a specified joint. Across five training seeds and 3000 held-out test runs, SHAPE-CWT achieves a mean accuracy of 84.69 percent, versus 81.67 percent for torque residuals and 97.17 percent for the generalized momentum observer under common CWT processing. The respective sample standard deviations are 0.70, 0.70, and 0.37 percentage points. These results demonstrate useful fault-type discrimination from algebraic power residuals, while severity-excitation profiles and offline velocity perturbations reveal limits to their diagnostic capability.

papers.abstract: Radiative heat transfer plays a dominant role in fire simulations, where solving the radiative transfer equation (RTE) is a computational bottleneck. Neural operators can accelerate these computations by learning solution operators from offline simulation data. However, conventional DeepONet surrogates rely on fixed-grid inputs and affine reconstruction, limiting their flexibility across resolutions and their approximation accuracy at a fixed latent dimension. In this paper, we develop a transformer-based DeepONet for multi-resolution RTE surrogate modelling. The proposed approach combines a Perceiver encoder, which maps temperature and absorption coefficient fields at different spatial resolutions into a fixed-size latent representation, with a cross-attention decoder that enables non-affine reconstruction of the radiative intensity. This architecture allows a single model to process inputs at varying resolutions without resampling them onto a common grid. We formulate a computable empirical version of a previously derived theoretical lower bound for affine reconstruction, enabling direct comparison with model errors on the same dataset. Experiments on a two-dimensional pool-fire dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms autoencoder-based DeepONets in predicting both radiative intensity and incident radiation, with fewer trainable parameters. Power spectral density analysis shows improved preservation of small-scale structures. Both affine baselines remain above the corresponding lower bound at all evaluated ranks, whereas the proposed model achieves a training error below it at one matched latent dimension, demonstrating the potential of non-affine reconstruction to overcome this representational limitation. Experiments on a dataset combining three spatial resolutions confirm the accuracy advantage of the approach at each input resolution.

papers.title: HA-DiPO: Diffusion Policy Optimization for Heterogeneous Cooperative Transport
papers.abstract: Cooperative transport with heterogeneous legged robots requires coordinating different motion capabilities while supporting an unfixed shared payload. We present HA-DiPO (Heterogeneous-Agent Diffusion Policy Optimization), a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE). The framework decouples team-level coordination from embodiment-specific motion control: at the high level, a centralized critic uses team-value estimates to jointly train independent coordination policies, aligning robot-specific action responses with a shared transport objective; at the low level, embodiment-specific robust motion policies track the coordination commands. The high-level diffusion policies offer more flexible action distributions than single-Gaussian parameterizations, allowing potentially multimodal coordination responses to be represented. The coordination policies learn from scratch through reward-driven simulator interaction without demonstrations. At execution, each robot generates coordination commands using only local robot and payload observations, without partner-state inputs or inter-robot messages. Simulation comparisons show that HA-DiPO achieves higher final mean returns and velocity-tracking success rates, as well as lower velocity errors, than the evaluated baselines. Real-world experiments further demonstrate quadrupedal-wheeled-legged and human-robot cooperative transport.

papers.title: Hybrid-time PINNs: Discontinuity-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Learning Hybrid Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Hybrid dynamical systems flow continuously but jump at discrete events. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) fit data while enforcing known dynamics, but a single network is smooth in time and cannot model these jumps. We show that the more closely a PINN follows a jump, the larger its physics loss must be. We propose hybrid-time PINNs (HT-PINNs), which assign one network to each flow interval of the hybrid time domain and train the networks jointly with the jump times and the unknown parameters. The number of jumps and the sequence of modes are found by enumeration. HT-PINNs recover the number of jumps and the restitution coefficient of a bouncing ball. In a MuJoCo simulation of robotic disassembly, where a robot pulls a press-fitted pin out of a housing through a spring, HT-PINNs find the number of jumps and the sequence of modes, and estimate the static and kinetic friction coefficients with small errors of 0.1% and 1.7%.

papers.title: Climate downscaling with likelihood functional flow matching
papers.abstract: Decisions about heat, frost and flooding are made locally, yet reanalyses and climate models resolve tens of kilometres. Generative downscalers add kilometre-scale detail with uncertainty, but are tied to a grid, costly to sample and lack a tractable likelihood. Here we introduce CD-FFM, a functional flow-matching model that treats the high-resolution field as a continuous random field that one model can query at any location and resolution. Its velocity acts pointwise, so spatial variability comes from a noise prior fitted to the observed spectrum and every observation has an exact likelihood. Downscaling ERA5 to 1 km daily temperature over Fennoscandia, CD-FFM lowers the continuous ranked probability score by 27-31% against regression and 12-18% against a forty-times larger neural operator in each of three test years, and outperforms a CorrDiff-style diffusion model while sampling about fifty times faster. The same model transfers to precipitation and makes large kilometre-scale ensembles affordable.

papers.title: FG-ConvNO: A Geometry-Aware Neural Operator for Propeller CFD Prediction
papers.abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is essential in contemporary engineering design, yet it remains expensive to compute and can take thousands of CPU/GPU hours or more for a single high-fidelity simulation. Recent developments in machine learning for scientific modeling have led to powerful surrogate frameworks that can approximate flow fields and physical quantities by using a fraction of the computational cost. However, most of these methods require largescale homogeneous datasets or simple geometries, exhibiting severe generalization gaps when applied to complex and data-scarce configurations. To address this, we propose the Factorized Geometry Convolutional Neural Operator (FG-ConvNO) for robust geometry-aware propeller pressure prediction under limited training data. We introduce geometryaware encoding, efficient interpolation-based decoding, and auxiliary global quantity supervision. In addition, we incorporate DISCO blocks that use discrete continuous convolutions to make the model discretization agnostic. In our experiments, FG-ConvNO achieves the highest accuracy for both surface pressure and global thrust prediction on a procedurally generated propeller CFD dataset. Geometry-aware encoding and architectural simplification improve stability, while random vertex subsampling enhances robustness. Overall, adding geometric priors to grid-based convolutional operators reduces overfitting on complex propeller geometries and improves generalization in low-data regimes.

papers.title: Advanced 3D bioprinting of cell-laden bioinks for neural tissue engineering
papers.abstract: Nerve injuries, including peripheral nerve injury (PNI) and central nervous system injury, remain challenging due to the limitations of conventional approaches in recreating the complex neural microenvironment and practical constraints such as donor-site morbidity and immune-related risks. Recent advances in 3D bioprinting enable spatial control over biomaterials, cells, and biochemical cues, facilitating the fabrication of biomimetic, cell-laden hydrogel scaffolds for experimental neural tissue engineering. Neural tissue engineering studies often incorporate neuro-supportive or neuroactive cell types, such as Schwann cells and neural stem cells, together with tailored bioink formulations to modulate neurite outgrowth, cell–material interactions, and signaling-associated processes. This review summarizes progress in 3D bioprinting with emphasis on cell-derived bioinks and printing-related design parameters across extrusion-based, droplet-based, and photolithography-based strategies. However, the evidence base is heterogeneous: outcomes vary across in vitro models, defect paradigms, biomaterials, cell sources, controls, and endpoints. Therefore, reported improvements should be interpreted primarily as scaffold and bioink performance within specific experimental contexts rather than as direct proof of clinically established therapeutic superiority. Finally, we highlight translational bottlenecks, including reproducible manufacturing, immunological safety, and clinically meaningful comparative benchmarks, to guide future actionable research.

papers.title: Dexterous ball balancing with robot arm manipulator using deep reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Ball-balancing on a robotic manipulator is a challenging control problem due to its nonlinear dynamics, underactuation, instability, and stringent safety requirements. Although Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has achieved notable success in robotic control, developing solutions that are simultaneously safe, robust, and adaptable remains an open challenge. In this work, we investigate ball-balancing on a 7-DoF robotic arm using the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm. We first compare SAC with DDPG, TD3, and PPO under identical training conditions, evaluating their learning performance and stability. SAC demonstrates the most stable and reliable learning behavior and is therefore selected as the baseline approach. Building on SAC, we introduce a control barrier-inspired reward shaping strategy that discourages unsafe states while preserving balancing performance. We further extend the framework through transfer learning to address a dynamic ball-catching task. Robustness is assessed through zero-shot generalization experiments involving variations in ball mass, radius, and initial placement. The resulting policies achieve consistent stabilization with an approximate settling time of 4 s, while the safety-aware policy remains within the prescribed spatial boundary under the evaluated simulation conditions. The learned controller remains effective despite ball mass changes exceeding an order of magnitude and ball radii ranging from 1 mm to 21 mm. These results highlight the potential of the proposed SAC-based framework for achieving safe, transferable, and robust robotic manipulation.

papers.abstract: Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) is an indicator of phytoplankton biomass but is not continuously measured at all water-quality monitoring sites. This study evaluated machine learning models for estimating Chl-a from routinely monitored water-quality variables, focusing on temporal validation, evaluation at a single external site, and reduced input availability. Hourly data from 12 South Korean monitoring sites (2021–2025) were used to develop Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, LightGBM, and Extra Trees (ET) models, optimized using Bayesian optimization and five-fold cross-validation. XGBoost achieved the highest random-split internal R2 (0.9219), whereas RF had the highest external-site R2 point estimate at Yangpyeong (0.6928). However, temporal validation using 2025 data yielded substantially lower R2 values (0.3528–0.5255), indicating reduced predictive performance in a subsequent period. SHAP analysis identified dissolved oxygen and pH as the leading contributors to RF predictions. At Yangpyeong, excluding total nitrogen and total phosphorus produced an R2 of 0.6897 versus 0.6928 with all inputs, with no clear difference detected by paired block bootstrap analysis; excluding turbidity reduced performance. These findings suggest the potential for supplementary Chl-a estimation with reduced inputs at Yangpyeong and provide a basis for further transferability assessments at additional monitoring sites.

papers.title: Curriculum-Driven Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Far-Range Rocket Landing
papers.abstract: Autonomous vertical landing of reusable launch vehicles is a critical yet formidable challenge in aerospace engineering, primarily due to highly nonlinear dynamics, stringent precision require- ments, and inherent environmental uncertainties. While reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising alternative to traditional model-based control, existing approaches frequently rely on flat training paradigms and highly simplified initial conditions, drastically limiting their real-world applicability. This paper proposes a comprehensive curriculum-driven deep reinforcement learning framework designed to master both far-range navigation and precision landing. By employing a three-stage curriculum augmented with a critic warm-up procedure and a rehearsal mechanism to prevent catastrophic forgetting, alongside a high-dimensional observation vector utilizing a full 3 X 3 rotation-matrix, the agent is trained to navigate from an initial horizontal distance of 1,000 to 1,500 units vastly farther than prior benchmarks before executing a soft touchdown. Crucially, we intro- duce a redesigned reward function that reduces unnecessary computational overhead and addresses limitations of earlier formulations, including poorly calibrated reward components and potentially conflicting optimization objectives. The redesigned function bounds the per-step reward magnitude by (O(1)), while its progress term accumulates the total distance closed over the trajectory. The available 100,000-episode results report a 99.98% success rate for the proposed policy and 68.31% for the baseline under the evaluation conditions. In the evaluation, the proposed policy retained 69.1% of its initial fuel capacity and achieved a mean final distance from the pad centre of 7.07 units, compared with 13.10 units for the baseline. Landing visualizations are available in Video 1 and Video 2.

papers.title: Peer-led examination simulation reshapes psychophysiological and emotional state profiles during problem-based medical learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Problem-based learning is widely assumed to activate students through self-directed inquiry, collaborative reasoning, and contextualized problem solving, yet the psychophysiological and achievement-emotional state dynamics generated by regular PBL sessions remain poorly characterized. In particular, familiar PBL routines may not always provide sufficient salience, accountability, or retrieval-related activation to fully engage the learner states they are intended to promote. This repeated-measures study examined whether embedding a peer-led examination simulation into regular PBL reshapes students’ psychophysiological and achievement-emotional state profiles during medical learning. Forty-two medical students were assessed across resting baseline, regular PBL, and PBL with peer-led examination simulation. Heart rate variability was recorded during two 5-minute performance intervals per learning condition and analyzed using RMSSD, SDNN, pNN50, and LF/HF ratio. Psychological measures captured social interaction anxiety, perceived stress, state anxiety, achievement emotions, self-rated performance, and post-session appraisal. Both PBL formats reduced heart rate variability relative to baseline, indicating that regular PBL itself constituted an autonomically active learning state. Compared with regular PBL, peer-led examination simulation induced additional HRV withdrawal, reflected by lower RMSSD, SDNN, and pNN50, whereas LF/HF did not show a robust condition effect. Baseline-adjusted interval-level mixed models replicated the examination-simulation effect for RMSSD, SDNN, and pNN50. At the achievement-emotional level, the simulation increased anxiety and perceived stress while reducing boredom. Enjoyment, motivation, and self-rated performance remained stable. Students also reported greater perceived benefit from, and stronger preference for, the examination-simulation format. Exploratory analyses further indicated that stronger increases in anxiety were associated with stronger additional RMSSD withdrawal, suggesting convergence between achievement-emotional activation and autonomic regulation. These findings show that peer-led examination simulation does not merely add stress to PBL, but shifts the learning episode toward a more salient, assessment-like, and educationally valued psychophysiological state without compromising students’ motivation. More broadly, the study positions psychophysiological measurement as a tool for examining how instructional design modulates achievement-emotional dynamics, attentional engagement, and autonomic regulation during authentic medical learning.

papers.title: Beyond point predictions: Uncertainty-aware timber compressive strength estimation using machine learning and conformal prediction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable estimation of compressive strength parallel to the grain is important for timber grading and structural assessment, yet the natural heterogeneity of solid timber limits the information provided by deterministic point predictions. This study develops an uncertainty-aware machine learning-conformal prediction (ML-CP) framework for solid sawn Radiata Pine. The development database comprised 491 compression specimens from 175 parent boards and was represented using two acoustic NDT-based feature sets (FS-MTG and FS-HM) and one density-based feature set (FS-DEN), all incorporating common moisture content and knot variables. Five tree-based ML models and five CP variants were evaluated over 30 repeated board-wise splits at a nominal 90% coverage level. CatBoost with FS-MTG achieved the strongest mean test-set point-prediction performance, with (R 2 = 0.842 ± 0.043), RMSE (= 4.812 ± 0.549) MPa, and MAE (= 3.771 ± 0.419) MPa. Relative to FS-DEN, FS-MTG and FS-HM reduced model-averaged RMSE by 8.8% and 5.8%, respectively, demonstrating the added predictive value of acoustic dynamic stiffness. Naive CP produced the narrowest intervals but systematically under-covered, with an aggregate mean empirical coverage (EC) of 0.741. In contrast, Jackknife+ and CV+ achieved mean EC values of 0.912 and 0.925 with mean interval widths (MIW) of 17.840 and 18.402 MPa, respectively, while the minmax variants provided greater coverage at the cost of wider intervals. SHAP and partial dependence analyses identified KAR as the dominant predictor and showed physically consistent effects of dynamic modulus, density, moisture content, knot location, and knot type. Application to 20 specimens from six external boards further illustrated how prediction intervals and lower bounds may support conservative strength screening of new material.

papers.title: Rapid Pedestrian-Level Wind Prediction Across Urban Building Layouts Using a Geometry-Conditioned Multi-Scale Neural Operator
papers.abstract: Convolutional and neural-operator surrogates enable rapid urban wind prediction, but their apparent accuracy can depend on physical-scale inconsistencies, related-layout leakage, and the mixture of idealized and realistic cases. The scientific question is whether a geometry-conditioned local–spectral model provides a reproducible improvement once these evaluation risks are controlled, and whether that improvement persists in realistic neighborhoods. We combine an audited UrbanTALES representation, grouped evaluation, and Geo-MSO to predict two-dimensional pedestrian-level velocity statistics and turbulent kinetic energy. The 538 cases comprise 224 idealized and 314 realistic configurations; inputs use fixed physical windows and targets are normalized by friction velocity. On 81 geometry-held-out cases, Geo-MSO achieved a wind-speed MAE of 0.1275 ± 0.0005 m s−1, with baseline-relative mean reductions of 2.15% versus U-Net and 6.62% versus FNO. However, among the 47 realistic test cases, it outperformed FNO in only 51.1%, with a median FNO-minus-Geo-MSO difference of approximately 0.00010 m s−1. Aggregate improvement therefore does not establish consistent realistic-domain superiority. All eight primary error diagnostics favored Geo-MSO over FNO across three seeds, whereas most U-Net paired intervals included zero. Unequal parameter counts and conditioning also prevent attribution to a single architectural component. Idealized pretraining accelerated target convergence without improving final realistic accuracy; narrow street-canyon jets remained underpredicted. Measured end-to-end inference took 0.114–1.747 s on an RTX 4090 D. The empirical contribution is a reproducible, morphology-qualified assessment of a combined model-and-evaluation pipeline, supporting preliminary screening rather than peak-wind certification or replacement of validated CFD.

papers.title: From Detection to Prediction: A Systematic Review of Intelligent Fault Detection in Industrial Conveyor Belt Systems
papers.abstract: Industrial conveyor belt systems are critical infrastructure where unexpected failures cause major downtime, safety hazards, and economic losses, motivating growing research on AI-based fault detection. However, previous reviews have either focused on a single sensing modality, particularly computer vision, or considered conveyor systems within broader mining applications, without jointly assessing methodological quality, cross-modal sensing, deployment readiness, and the technical capabilities required for prognosis. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this review analyzes 131 empirical studies on intelligent fault detection in industrial conveyor belt systems published between 2010 and 2026, with particular attention to sensing technologies, AI-based analytical methods, and deployment feasibility. The analysis considers the main fault types reported in the literature and the sensors and algorithms used for their detection. Deep learning was the dominant analytical approach (55.0% of studies), with CNN-based architectures such as YOLO, ResNet, and U-Net widely used for vision-based applications, while LSTM and GRU models were more commonly applied to acoustic and vibration signals. Vision/camera sensing accounted for 40.5% of studies, and mining represented 74% of applications. Despite substantial progress in automated fault detection, most studies remain focused on identifying existing faults rather than anticipating future degradation. Remaining useful life was estimated in only three studies (2.3%) and degradation trends in seven (5.3%); physics-informed machine learning and cross-site domain adaptation were absent, and principled multi-sensor fusion, uncertainty quantification, explainability, and digital-twin integration each appeared in no more than six studies. Predictive uncertainty was quantified in only one study (0.8%), and its calibration was not demonstrated. Future advances should therefore place greater emphasis on prognosis, cross-site generalization, uncertainty-aware inference, explainable models, and principled sensor fusion to support more reliable and transferable predictive maintenance systems.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow in a Channel with Isothermal Staggered Wall-Mounted Squares
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have been increasingly used for thermal-fluid problems. This study evaluates the performance of the PINN approach for reconstructing a laminar forced flow field inside a rectangular channel with four staggered wall-mounted squares. Air is used as the working fluid, at a Reynolds number of Re = 100 and a Prandtl number of Pr = 0.71. The four squares are isothermal at 80 °C while the inlet fluid temperature is 20 °C. The PINN is used to predict velocity, pressure and temperature fields, as well as local and average Nusselt numbers. The PINN solutions are verified against the reference finite volume solution with 262,400 control volumes. The finite volume method is validated against exact solutions for laminar flow between isothermal plates (Poiseuille flow and Graetz problem). The PINN was trained on 100, 250, 1000 and 4000 velocity and temperature sample points. Each case was trained five times with different random seeds. Without samples the PINN fails, with streamwise velocity and temperature errors equal to 49% and 137%, respectively. With 1000 uniformly placed samples throughout the domain, the streamwise and cross-stream velocity errors are 0.5% and 2.9%, respectively. The error of the pressure predicted by the network is 0.9% while the error in the temperature field is 1.6%. The average Nusselt number is underpredicted by 11% and increasing the sample count to 4000 points does not reduce this error. A significant improvement is obtained by placing sample points inside the thermal boundary layer of the isothermal squares. When 35% of the 1000 sample points are placed in the thermal boundary layer, the error in the average Nusselt number decreases to 8% and its scatter between the training runs is reduced by four times. The reconstructed fields are more accurate than linear, radial basis function and Kriging interpolation of the same samples.

papers.title: Adjuvant phage therapy in periprosthetic joint infection: comparative analysis of medium-term treatment results
papers.abstract: Introduction Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is one of the major complications following primary and revision total hip arthroplasty, accounting for 15–25 % of revision procedures. PJI caused by multidrug-resistant microorganisms is associated with a higher risk of recurrence and severe consequences, including loss of limb function and amputation. The growing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among staphylococci and Gram-negative bacteria, further complicates the PJI treatment. Purpose To conduct a comparative analysis of the mid-term results of adjuvant phage therapy in combination with standard therapy in patients with periprosthetic hip joint infection caused by multidrug-resistant microorganisms. Materials and Methods The study was designed as a non-randomized, open-label, prospective study that included 39 patients with chronic periprosthetic hip joint infection (hip PJI). All patients underwent appropriate surgical treatment and were divided into two groups: the study group ( n = 19), in which personalized phage therapy was used in combination with targeted antibiotic therapy, and the comparison group ( n = 20), which received antibiotic therapy alone. The median follow-up period was at least 120 weeks; the recurrence rate was assessed after 104 weeks. The primary criterion for treatment efficacy was eradication of PJI and the absence of PJI recurrence within 104 weeks after revision arthroplasty. Results The odds of PJI recurrence within 104 weeks of follow-up in the study group were five times lower than in the comparison group ( OR = 0.2), with recurrence rates of 10.5 % and 45.0 %, respectively ( p = 0.031). The study group demonstrated significantly higher implant survival compared with the comparison group: implant survival at 104 weeks reached 89 % and 55 %, respectively. The mean risk ratio for implant loss in the David Cox proportional hazards model was 0.17 (log-rank test, p = 0.012). The study group also showed a significantly higher proportion of recovered patients compared with the comparison group, with rates of 89.5 % and 55.0 %, respectively ( OR = 6.3; p = 0.031). Discussion The results obtained for the causative PJI agents are consistent with the data in the literature. Both groups were dominated by cefoxime-resistant forms of staphylococci as a marker antibiotic, which reflects the PJI patterns of development in arthroplasty. The use of antibacterial drugs in large doses for eradication of pathogenic bacteria in biofilms leads to the accumulation of mutations in the genomes of the causative PJI agents, which is the reason for the development of drug resistance and recurrence of infection. The use of alternative therapies for PJI, in particular phage therapy, may change the treatment strategy. Adjuvant phage therapy has potential in the PJI caused by antibiotic-resistant pathogens. Conclusion Adjuvant phage therapy combined with antibiotic therapy is an effective treatment modality for periprosthetic hip joint infection caused by multidrug-resistant pathogens and may significantly reduce the recurrence rate of periprosthetic infection and thereby improve clinical outcomes. Further large randomized studies are required to confirm our findings and to use this method.
